openPoints: When Promise.race times out, what aborts the underlying resourceRead so repeated permanently hung transports cannot accumulate physical network work even though logical lookup capacity has been released?

Where are the client-side active, timeout, completion, and max-latency aggregates exported to operational telemetry, given that the navigator instance currently retains them behind an internal metrics method?
How will the fixed ten-second timeout be calibrated for high-latency deployments so it protects capacity without turning healthy slow reads into cached false failures?
architectureTip: Carry an abort signal through the point-read transport and publish identifier-free pool metrics through the existing operational telemetry boundary.
topFinding: Retry #2 closes all prior correctness and boundedness findings at the application layer: timeouts and generation-local pools reclaim capacity, stale completions remain inert, strict safe-integer/domain/level validation and drive-relative redaction hold, failure throttling is generation-scoped, and identifier-free tail metrics are recorded; only transport-level cancellation and metrics export remain as resilience hardening.
